chapter: War years, Decca records and La Conga
title: Marcelino Guerra brought to New York
summary: Mario recommended Guerra, top composer in Cuba then singing with Arsenio Rodriguez, to Robbins; Machito compares him to Lecuona.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Okay. I know I learned from you that Marcelino Guerra came to the United States in 1943. Jack Robbins sent for him. On whose recommendation did......

Mario Bauza. At that time, I noticed that there was a big surge to record Latin music with English titles like "Perfidia", "Frenesi", "Amor", "The Breeze and I", all of those things. Is this one of the reasons why Marcelino Guerra came to the United States?
Possibly, because with all the respect of (Ernesto) Lecuona

and all those big composers that we had from Cuba and Puerto Rico, like Rafael Hernandez and Pedro Flores, Marcelino Guerra could be included. I mean, popular music, I can't compare Marcelino Guerra with Lecuona because Lecuona was a concert pianist, he was top-ten in his time, when he was young, and he was a semi-classic composer and classic composer; but naturally, he played, he wrote "Panama" and "Say Si Si", all those popular tunes that he did that in his spare moments.

So, in that particular style, Marcelino was as good as Lecuona. That's why Mario recommend Marcelino Guerra to Jack Robbins: "Why don't you bring Marcelino Guerra, he is a great composer"? As a matter of fact, Marcelino Guerra was the top composer in Cuba.
.....in 1943. Was Marcelino singing with any band or doing any.....
Yes, he was singing with Arsenio Rodriguez.
Ohh!!, he was singing with Arsenio at that time.
With Arsenio. All right, so he came in 1943. Do you remember what he did when he arrived here?
